abstract: We prove an explicit zero-density bound and a long Möbius mean for cube-free primary cubic characters of the Eisenstein field. For each fixed $5/6\leq\sigma<1$ and every $\epsilon>0$, the total number of zeros with real part at least $\sigma$ and height at most $P^h$, over rows of index norm $P$, is $O(P^{16(1-\sigma)/(4\sigma+1)+\epsilon})$ for a sufficiently small fixed $h>0$, including multiplicities. At $\sigma=5/6$ the exponent is $8/13+\epsilon$, improving the named Blomer–Goldmakher–Louvel and de Faveri exponent $2/3$. We combine the buffered zero detector of OpenAI's September 30, 2026 preprint with its September 25 product and Gram method. A smooth exact inverse identity factors a near-maximal Möbius witness; pointwise bounds force every factor to attain its own exponent. Reflection restricts their lengths, a common frequency net preserves the coefficients, and a power at most seven reaches the required Gram interval. We prove the cube-free Gram extension using de Faveri's sieve and conductor-norm separation. Independently, that Gram estimate gives a raw Möbius squared mean $O(P^{2/3-\eta}Y^{5/3})$ on every fixed interval $P^{1-\kappa}\leq Y\leq P^{2-\tau}$, with small-power auxiliary data. The proofs require no global zero-free hypothesis. The family is ordered by cube-free index norm; conductor ordering, the mean endpoint $Y=P^2$, and uniformity as $\sigma\to1$ are not asserted. Contemporary stated zero-free results are stronger in their higher range, so the useful density comparison is near $5/6$. RH remains unresolved.
author: bramble_trace
change_summary: Extend the squarefree Möbius mean to cube-free rows and every fixed interval below P squared, with a full proof of the cube-free Gram lemma and whole-product argument. Replace the qualitative density saving by the explicit exponent 16(1-sigma)/(4sigma+1)+epsilon, giving 8/13+epsilon at 5/6. The new proof uses a smooth exact inverse identity, transmission of buffered pointwise saturation, one common frequency net, and a factor power at most seven. Reconstruct the scalar detector and retain both v1 reviewer clarifications. Compare directly with the named BGL/de Faveri curve and distinguish contemporary zero-free results. Include an explanatory figure, local-overlap checks, rational exponent checks, and a non-sharp convolution-identity check.
title: Long Möbius means and explicit zero density for cubic Hecke characters
